title: A second, all-human proof the same afternoon
happened: Around four hours after the note, posts began linking a blog post by the president of the American Mathematical Society: a separate, all-human proof of the generalised hypothesis by a mathematician named Alessandro Masullo, which a colleague had been reviewing for months and which was put out early, unpolished, because of the first announcement. The community read the two side by side. zuko-always-lies, a 111-follower account, worked out that if both check out the human one does it in 0.4% of the pages; sciortino replied that he trusted a giant inscrutable Lean proof more than a readable 900-page human one. Others called it the last time John Henry beats the steam engine, asked who does responsible disclosure for math 0-days, wondered what 'all-human' means if the humans used computers, and hoped both proofs were true. norvid proposed, as a film, two AI-assisted mathematicians releasing increasingly daring proofs in bitter mutual combat; a reply asked for secret twins, and yonderdavid pointed out that the colleague reviewing the human proof is one of a pair of identical-twin mathematicians. By late evening members were relaying that people trying to formalise the human proof in Lean were finding gaps, and that the mood among mathematicians leaned towards the machine proof holding and the human one not. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.

alts:
Screenshot of a chat message from Patrick:

It looks like in fact the proof has significant gaps and the formalization effort has stalled on those gaps: https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo

"On hold (20 November 2026). The paper's main theorem, the trace formula of Theorem 12.5.1.1, is in dispute. In the Lean Zulip thread Formalising Masullo's proof of GRH it was reported that an LLM-assisted reading found a counterexample to it, and that correcting one of the errors reduces the theorem to a classical formula. The details have not been posted, and others in the thread consider a formalization premature. The draft is also incomplete: Chapter 13, which should deduce GRH, has no statement of its main theorem."
